why: Route-A cap 3 is A61's original token, sized from measured RSS (about 10.5 GB route-A baseline plus 0.40 GiB per worker at K_big 128). For the 10-run headline batch it gives 7.23 h E / 15.55 h U against 7.23 / 12.97 h for V005 cap 6 and 12.73 / 25.52 h for the orchestrator-style budget 16 (fluid model, 18 cores).

Cap 6 buys 17% in the upper case but lets modelled free memory fall to 15.8% (below the gate, after admission) with 44.5 busy processes on 18 cores; cap 3 keeps it at or above 31.1% for the headline batch.

The budget-16 accounting counts 2 busy processes for every call in route B, so it caps a batch at about 5 concurrent calls and adds 5.5-10.0 h to the critical path; it suits the campaign (where it is the reviewed rule) but not the short direct batches.

Memory gate 25%, 60 s poll, one start per poll and the first-iteration ramp are the reviewed V005 rules (A72 ITEM3-R1; Claude4 0076 ramp 14/14). The first iteration completes about 12.6 min (tail-ON) / 7.8 min (tail-OFF) after start, solo.
Campaign m=6 (the nominal wave size) under the existing budget 17 gives 8.7 d E / 14.9 d U against 26.0 / 43.8 d at the shipped max_concurrent 1; no code change.
